title: Tovera-led La Salle wins 3rd straight as rival Ateneo falls in OT thriller
summary: Super rookie Joaquin Tovera shines with a heroic performance as La Salle trumps rival Ateneo in overtime to stay undefeated in the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament second round

image.caption: Tovera-led La Salle wins 3rd straight as rival Ateneo falls in OT thriller

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – La Salle rookie Joaquin Tovera again stayed ahead of his learning curve in the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament as he led the Green Archers to a thrilling 76-73 overtime escape of rivals Ateneo Blue Eagles at the Araneta Coliseum on Saturday, October 31.

Before succumbing to a non-contact ankle roll in the final minute of a heated extra period, Tovera willed La Salle with game-highs of 21 points and 6 assists to go with 7 rebounds as the Green Archers broke a standings deadlock with the Blue Eagles to go third at 6-4.
Veteran guard JC Macalalag led a balanced scoring effort behind Tovera with 11 points in nearly 39 minutes of action, as six other La Salle players tallied at least 5 points.
“When the game went to overtime, we just reminded everybody about what we discussed before the game and we talked about our dreams,” said Archers head coach Topex Robinson.
“In every moment, the strongest dream will win that moment, so we all dream about playing in the De La Salle-Ateneo rivalry. These guys just showed up and they believed in what we prepared for.”

Ateneo young stars Jared Bahay and super rookie Kieffer Alas paced the heartbreaking loss with 18 points apiece — with all their efforts nullified as they failed to link up on a basic inbounds pass that gave the ball back to the Green Archers with 3.3 seconds left in overtime.

Shawn Tuano added 12 points and 6 rebounds, while Travis Roberts likewise scored 12 on a 5-of-17 clip, as the Blue Eagles tripped down a 5-5 slate for fifth place in a hyper-competitive field still featuring seven realistic Final Four contenders.

In the previous game of the loaded double-header, the NU Bulldogs strengthened its hold of second place with a scrappy 75-71 escape of the reeling UST Growling Tigers for a 7-3 record — half a game behind 7-2 UP.

Head coach Jeff Napa once again worked his magic on big men as star foreign student-athlete Mo Diassana tallied a huge 16-point, 19-rebound double-double, backstopped by 14 markers and 6 boards in just 15 minutes from MVP candidate PJ Palacielo.

Burly big Kenshin Padrones added his own double-double of 13 points and 12 rebounds, while Tebol Garcia topscored the NU back court with 12 points, 7 boards, and a game-high 6 assists, making up for MVP frontrunner Reinhard Jumamoy’s lackluster 6-point showing.
Amiel Acido and Mark Llemit paced the losing cause with 13 and 12 points, respectively, while star center Collins Akowe was limited to 11 points on 2-of-7 shooting with just 5 rebounds in 33 minutes.
Amid a heavily-contested elimination round, UST plummeted to a 4-6 card at seventh place with a costly third straight loss, while still being just two games behind No. 3 La Salle.
